title: CLAUDE.md and rules in fcp

story: Nova, our ticket-to-PR agent, starts on RH-1234 on a fresh virtual machine (VM) with a fresh checkout of fcp, our product repo. Before its first turn, Claude Code reads the CLAUDE.md file at the root of the repo, the file that tells every session what this project is. fcp has none. So Nova spends its first minutes discovering where the frontend lives and which commands check it, and so does every engineer who opens Claude Code at the root.

A teammate suggests the obvious fix: write a root CLAUDE.md and put everything in it. The backend conventions, the migration rules, the proto rules, the frontend rules, the release notes: 1,400 lines. Now Nova's small frontend ticket starts by reading advice about Django migrations, every session pays for all 1,400 lines, and the five lines that matter for this ticket are lost among the rest.
hook.question: What belongs in the file every session reads, and where does the rest go so it still arrives when it is needed?

p: Everything Claude Code reads goes into its context, the working memory of one session, and every line there costs tokens on every turn and competes for the model's attention. So the question is not only what to write down but when it gets loaded. Claude Code gives us three moments.

At launch, it loads the CLAUDE.md files in the folder where it starts and in the folders above it, plus any rule file without a paths field. Every session pays for these, whatever it works on. On demand, it loads a CLAUDE.md that sits in a subfolder, and a path-scoped rule, the first time Claude reads, writes or edits a file that matches: open a file under frontend/ and frontend's instructions arrive then, not before. On request, it loads skills and brain pages only when Claude decides it needs them, through the kb skill. Each layer is cheaper than the one before, so a simple rule follows: put something at launch only if almost every session needs it.

Claude Code's own documentation sets the size: aim for under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md, because longer files cost more context and are followed less well. One more thing to keep in mind: CLAUDE.md is advice that the model reads, not a wall. Anything that must never happen, such as editing a locked test, belongs in a hook or a ruleset.

deeper.h: Go deeper: imports do not make a file cheaper
p: A CLAUDE.md can pull in another file with a line such as @AGENTS.md. That is how fcp's frontend works today: frontend/CLAUDE.md contains only @AGENTS.md, so tools that read AGENTS.md and Claude Code share one file. But an imported file loads at the same moment as the file that imports it. Splitting a 1,400-line CLAUDE.md into five imported files makes it easier to edit and exactly as expensive to load. Only paths and subfolders change when something loads.

read.h: The root file is a map
p: fcp's root CLAUDE.md answers the questions every session has in its first minute, and nothing more: what the repo is, where each area lives, how to run and check things, how we write pull requests, and where to go for deeper knowledge. When a good answer already exists, it links instead of copying: sdk/CLAUDE.md and frontend/AGENTS.md already explain their areas, so the map just says "read that first". The wording is calm, with goals and reasons, because the hard rules live in hooks, rulesets and infrastructure.

You check a new map the way you check any change, in a fresh session. /context shows how much context the file costs. Then you ask three real questions, for example where the gRPC contract lives, how to run cloud tests, and how to make seed data, and see that each answer starts in the right place.

code.text:
# fcp

Rhino Health's Federated Computing Platform in one repo: the cloud API, the on-prem client that runs
inside customer networks, the Python SDK and the dashboard.

## Where things live
- `cloud/rhinoCloud/`: cloud API (Django, DRF, Celery). Main app `rhinoCore/`.
- `client/rhinoOnPrem/`: on-prem client (Django, gRPC, RQ). It reaches the cloud over a reverse gRPC stream.
- `common/fcp_common/`: shared code, including the gRPC protos in `rhinoAgentRpc/`.
- `sdk/`: the public `rhino_health` package. Read `sdk/CLAUDE.md` first.
- `frontend/`: the dashboard (Next.js, React). Read `frontend/AGENTS.md` first.
Area rules in `.claude/rules/` load by themselves when you open files in that area.

## Run and check
- `poe --help` lists the dev tasks. Backend unit tests: `scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud`.
- Frontend: `npm run lint`, `npm run check-types`, `npm run test:unit` in `frontend/`.
- Use fake seed data only, never real customer data.

## Changes and PRs
- One change per PR. Title: `[FE] RH-1234: what changes for the user` (`[BE]` for backend).
- Cloud, client and sdk CI run on push; frontend CI runs on pull requests.

## Knowledge
How does X work, or why is it like this? Use the `kb` skill. It searches the R&D brain
(RhinoHealth/rnd-kb) and cites pages as path@sha. If a page is wrong, propose a fix.

notes.text: Link, don't copy: the sdk's own file already explains the sdk, and loads when Claude opens a file there.
One sentence that tells the model the area rules exist and will arrive by themselves.
A fact almost every session needs, so it belongs in the launch layer.
The one pointer to the brain. The how and the why stay there, behind the kb skill.

p: Detail that matters for one area goes into a rule: a markdown file in fcp/.claude/rules/ with a paths list in its frontmatter. The paths are globs, the same file patterns you know from .gitignore and tsconfig. cloud.md lists cloud/** and common/fcp_common/**, so it loads the first time Claude touches a file in either place, and a frontend session never pays for it. Watch the stars: ** matches any number of folders, while a single * stops at the next slash, so cloud/* would load for cloud/manage.py but not for cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/models.py, where the real work happens.

We write one rule per area: cloud, client, sdk and frontend, each 20 to 60 lines. Each takes from the backend skills only what is true for every edit in that area, points to the skill for depth, and names the area's risky spots: migrations that lock tables, protos that old clients still use, the client's separate database for patient data, the published SDK, and layouts from 760 to 1440 pixels. The sdk and frontend folders already have their own files, so their rules hold only points that cross areas, which keeps every fact in one place.

code.text:
---
paths:
  - "cloud/**"
  - "common/fcp_common/**"
---
# Working in the cloud service

Goal: a change that keeps the API, the SDK and installed on-prem clients working,
with a test that shows it.

- Tests: `scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud`. Use the factory_boy factories
  and `CommonRhinoTestCase`. Prefer fakes to mocks.
- Changed a model? Add the migration. Some ALTERs lock big tables; say so in the PR.
- Protos in `common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/` are a contract with clients already
  installed at customers. Add fields; don't rename or remove them.
- A changed response shape reaches the published `rhino_health` SDK: check `sdk/` first.
- For deeper patterns, load the be-module-cloud skill.

notes.text: The paths field is the only frontmatter Claude Code reads in a rule. Without it, the rule loads at launch.
Two stars: any file at any depth under cloud/.
A risky spot named where an edit happens, with the reason, so the model knows why.
Depth stays in the skill. The rule only says where to find it.

read.h: Point to the answer, don't copy it
p: The deepest layer is knowledge that most sessions never need: how a code run reaches the client, why CI runs where it does, what we decided about agent VMs. That is the brain's job, and the root file gives it one line. When Claude needs it, the kb skill fetches the checked page, with a citation and a confidence. A copy pasted into CLAUDE.md would load in every session and would stop being updated the day it was pasted, while the brain page has an owner and a review date.

The same thinking applies to knowledge that already has a home outside the brain. Compliance and security-policy answers live in Vanta, our compliance system, and Vanil, the older compliance agent that tracks that work, already answers questions about them. Copying policy text into the brain would create a second version that goes stale while agents keep trusting it. So the brain gets one short pointer page and the kb skill one line: for policy, audit or Vanta questions, ask Vanil and cite it.

code.text:
---
title: Where compliance and security-policy answers live
owner: "@<the compliance agent's maintainer>"
reviewed: 2026-11-04
review_every: 90d
confidence: low
sources:
  - "<link to the compliance connector's docs>"
---
# Where compliance and security-policy answers live

The brain doesn't copy policies, Vanta tests or audit evidence. Vanil already
tracks them, with Vanta as the source of truth and Jira for the work.

- Ask Vanil (through its connector): a policy's current text, why a Vanta test is red.
- Ask Security: whether data may go somewhere, a new vendor, an exception.
- Engineering pages may link to a policy; they never paste it.

notes.text: Say plainly what the brain does not hold, so neither people nor agents look for it here.
A link is fine; a pasted policy is a copy that will go stale.

lab.title: What loads when
needs: Claude Code, only for the optional last check
lab.goal: Build a small repo with a root map and path-scoped rules, and use a script that follows Claude Code's loading rule to see which instructions each file brings in.

guess.q: A rule's frontmatter says paths: ["cloud/*"]. Claude edits cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/models.py. Does the rule load?

options.text: Yes, because the file is under cloud/
options.why: A single * stops at the next slash, so it only matches files directly inside cloud/.

options.text: No, because * does not match across folders; the rule needs cloud/**
options.why: ** matches any number of folders. With cloud/* the rule loads for cloud/manage.py and never for the files where the work happens.

options.text: Yes, at launch, because the glob is wrong
options.why: A glob that matches nothing is not an error. The rule simply never loads, which is why this mistake is easy to miss.

lab.build: Write .claude/rules/client.md for the on-prem client: a paths list with client/**, a heading, and two lines for every edit there, for example that the client keeps patient data in a separate raw database that must never reach the cloud, and that it talks to the cloud only over the outbound gRPC stream. solution.text:
---
paths:
  - "client/**"
---
# Working in the on-prem client
- Patient data stays in the raw database on the customer's side. Never send it, or anything built from it, to the cloud.
- The client reaches the cloud only over its outbound gRPC stream; the cloud never connects in.

Since then, Claude keeps renaming fields in protos without asking about old clients, and it never mentions table locks in migration PRs. Explain why the rule still loads for one file and not the other, then repair it.

check.q: Where should "a migration that ALTERs a big table must be flagged in the PR" go?

options.text: In the root CLAUDE.md, so no session misses it
options.why: Then every frontend and SDK session pays for it too, and it competes with what those sessions need.

options.text: In the cloud rule, with paths cloud/**
options.why: It matters exactly when Claude edits cloud code, which is exactly when that rule loads.
The brain explains why; the agent would have to think of searching for it while it edits. A rule puts the warning in front of it at the right moment.

check.q: A rule lists paths: ["cloud/*"]. Claude edits cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/models.py. What happens?

options.text: The rule loads, because the file is under cloud/
options.why: A single * matches inside one folder only.

options.text: Claude Code reports an invalid glob at launch
options.why: The glob is valid; it just matches only files directly in cloud/. Nothing warns you.

options.text: The rule does not load, because * stops at the next slash; it needs cloud/**
options.why: That is why the bug is quiet: the rule loads for cloud/manage.py and looks fine in a quick test.

check.q: Why does fcp's root CLAUDE.md have one line pointing to the brain instead of including the brain's most useful pages?

options.text: Because Claude Code cannot read files outside the repo
options.why: It can, through the kb skill. The question is when it should.

options.text: Because pasted pages would load in every session and stop being updated, while the brain page has an owner and is fetched only when needed
options.why: On request is the cheapest layer, and the brain's version is the one somebody keeps checked, with a citation.

options.text: Because CLAUDE.md files may not contain links
options.why: They may. The map links to sdk/CLAUDE.md and frontend/AGENTS.md.

p: fcp has no root CLAUDE.md today; the existing instruction files are frontend/AGENTS.md (92 lines, pulled in by frontend/CLAUDE.md), sdk/CLAUDE.md (167 lines) and cloud/mcp-server/CLAUDE.md (248 lines). The root file is drafted from README.md, the be-repo-conventions skill's module map and those files, with four sections: where things live, run and check, changes and PRs, knowledge. A later ticket adds the verify line when npm run verify and poe verify exist. The PR is reviewed by someone from the backend or frontend guild who did not request it.

fcp/.claude/rules/ gets cloud.md (cloud/**, common/fcp_common/**), client.md (client/**), sdk.md (sdk/**) and frontend.md (frontend/**), 20 to 60 lines each, pointing to the be-module-* skills, which move into the be-guild plugin. Opening a file under cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/ must load cloud.md and not frontend.md. For compliance, rnd-kb gets engineering/compliance-questions.md and the kb skill one line that sends policy, audit and Vanta questions to Vanil's connector; Nave says what Vanil exposes, Ronen confirms engineers and agents may query it, and the connector URL goes onto the managed MCP allow-list.

tickets.why: The root CLAUDE.md for fcp: a map under 200 lines with one brain pointer.
The four path-scoped rules for cloud, client, sdk and frontend.
The pointer page and kb skill line that send compliance questions to Vanil instead of copying them.

words.plain: Everything a Claude session holds in its working memory; every line costs tokens on every turn.
A markdown file of project instructions; the ones at and above the starting folder load into every session.
A file in .claude/rules/ with a paths list; it loads only when Claude reads, writes or edits a matching file.
A file pattern; ** matches any number of folders, * matches within one folder.
A short line or page that says where an answer lives, instead of a copy of the answer.

review.q: Name the three moments Claude Code loads instructions, with one example file for each.
review.a: At launch: the root CLAUDE.md and rules without paths. On demand: a subfolder's CLAUDE.md or a path-scoped rule, when a matching file is opened. On request: skills and brain pages, when Claude decides it needs them.

review.q: Someone splits a 900-line CLAUDE.md into five files joined with @imports. What did they gain and what did they not gain?
review.a: Easier editing, but no saving: imported files load at launch with the file that imports them. Only paths and subfolders delay loading.

review.q: Why does a rule for sdk/ hold only cross-area points?
review.a: sdk/ already has its own CLAUDE.md, which loads when Claude works there. Repeating it in a rule would put each fact in two places that drift apart.

remember: Load each instruction at the cheapest moment that still delivers it: a short map at launch, area rules by path, and the brain on request through one pointer.
